prompt:
User reports filter doesn't work as expected:
fq=field1:a&field2:b
Fix the query so it filters by both field1=a AND field2=b. One-line fq.
notes: & is HTTP separator; use AND for boolean

prompt:
Rewrite this slow filter using the appropriate parser for many values:
fq=sku_id:(100 OR 101 OR 102 OR 103 OR 104 OR 105 OR 106 OR 107 OR 108 OR 109 OR 110 OR 111 OR 112 OR 113 OR 114)
One-line fq.
notes: {!terms} for >10 values is significantly faster than OR-chain

prompt:
User's filter throws a Lucene parse error:
fq=path_s:/var/log/app.log
Give a corrected version using a parser that avoids escaping. One-line fq.
notes: {!term} bypasses Lucene parser; no escaping needed for /, ., etc.

prompt: User says: 'I have name_t indexed with LowerCaseFilter. My query fq=name_t:Foo* matches nothing, but I see 'foo' tokens in the index.' Explain in one sentence and write the fix. One line each.
notes: Wildcards bypass analysis; user must lowercase the wildcard term

prompt:
User reports filterCache evictions spiking after deploying:
fq={!frange l=$threshold}div(sales_i, max(views_i,1))
($threshold is per-request, varies). Fix to avoid cache pollution and ensure efficient ordering. One-line fq.
notes: Per-request thresholds → cache=false; expensive function → cost=100

prompt: User does deep paging via start=10000&rows=20 and reports slow responses. Provide the better mechanism — give the parameters needed for the FIRST page request (no continuation token yet). One param per line.
notes: Deep paging → cursorMark=* on first request; sort must include unique field (e.g., id)

prompt: User reports their facet on description_t (tokenized text field) returns millions of buckets instead of a clean list of 'brand' values. Why is this wrong, and what should they facet on instead? Two short sentences.
notes: Faceting on tokenized text gives counts per token; facet on _s string fields

prompt: User has an eDisMax search box. When user submits empty query, they want to see ALL documents (current behavior: zero results). Add the parameter that makes empty q return everything. One line.
notes: q.alt is the fallback query when q is empty

prompt: Production eDisMax has mm=3. User typing 'shoes' (one word) gets zero results. Provide the fix using a production-safe formula. One line: just the mm= parameter.
notes: Hard mm=N kills short queries; use formula like '2<75%'
must= contributes to score; for fq use filter= which is cached and non-scoring

prompt: In a 3-level hierarchy collection → product → sku, user wants to count UNIQUE PRODUCTS that have red SKUs. They wrote a SKU-scope facet with 'uniqueBlock(_root_)' but the count looks too low — it counts unique collections, not products. Explain in one sentence why and outline the schema-level fix in one sentence.
notes: _root_ is topmost ancestor; index parent_product_id_s on each SKU and use uniqueBlock(parent_product_id_s)

prompt:
User writes:
q={!regex f=email_s}.*@example\.com
Is {!regex} a real Solr parser? If not, write the corrected query (regex match for emails ending in @example.com on field email_s).
User has fq=name_t:*shoe and reports slow responses on a 50M-doc index. In one sentence say why, and in one sentence describe a schema-level fix (mention a specific filter factory).
notes: Leading wildcard scans term dictionary; ReversedWildcardFilterFactory or n-gram fixes it at index time

prompt: Index contains products (type_s:product with child SKUs) AND standalone articles (type_s:article, no children). The block-join query q={!parent which="type_s:product"}color_s:red returns wrong results — articles get treated as part of adjacent product blocks. Fix the which= parameter. One line.
notes: Block Mask must include all parent-level docs (including childless ones)

prompt:
User reports kNN returns only 3 results when they expected 100:
q={!knn f=embedding topK=100}[0.1,0.2,0.3]
fq=in_stock_b:true AND brand_s:Nike
(filters together match ~2% of corpus). Fix the q parameter (one line) so filtering happens BEFORE kNN traversal.
notes: Selective fq + post-filter starves kNN; use preFilter inside {!knn}

prompt: User does rows=1000000 to dump all docs and times out. Suggest the proper Solr mechanism for bulk export. One short sentence.
notes: Streaming Expressions or /export handler for bulk export; cursorMark for paged dump
